text:
Emily: :rotating_light: paging — we're seeing a sudden p99/Tail latency spike for streaming sessions in eu-west-2. p95 up from ~120ms to 2.1s, p99 hitting ~6.3s, streaming stalls and connection resets reported by the gateway.

incident-bot: INC-2026-345 created (severity P1). Alert rule: streaming_tail_latency > 3s for 5m. Notifying oncall.

Raj: looking now. graphs show packet loss counters rising on cross-zone NAT paths between az-b and az-c, and TLS handshake RTTs spiking. Could be routing or inter-AZ fabric issue.

Kevin: I'm on network. I see retransmits and occasional RST floods on the NAT gateway in eu-west-2a -> eu-west-2c. Ephemeral port exhaustion on the natX instance? hitting 64k-ish connections per worker.

Maria: customer impact: streaming sessions failing for ~4% of active streams in eu-west-2; throughput at 85% for dedicated customers. No data exfil. SLO risk: 30m window puts SLO breach possibility if not mitigated.

Emily: assign mitigations. Prioritize streaming tail: 1) divert new sessions to eu-west-1 (if capacity); 2) throttle/buffer retries; 3) increase NAT ephemeral ports / rotate NAT.

Raj: running quick query to see session locality: 
```
SELECT count(*) as c, az FROM sessions WHERE region='eu-west-2' GROUP BY az;
```
Results show 72% in az-b, 24% az-c, rest az-a.

Kevin: spinning up spare NAT in eu-west-2a and will update VPC route target for the problematic subnets. Also enabling connection re-use on gateway LB (keepalive tweaks). Exec steps:
```
# create new nat
aws ec2 allocate-address --domain vpc
aws ec2 create-nat-gateway --subnet-id subnet-xxxx --allocation-id eipalloc-xxxx
# update route table
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-xxxx --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-xxxx
```
ETA ~6-8m for route propagation.

Emily: @Kevin please annotate if we need fallback to divert to eu-west-1. Also start customer comms draft.

Kevin: route change pushed for two subnets (eu-west-2b, eu-west-2c). New nat-gateway active. Seeing drop in retransmits on those subnets. p95 trending down to 700ms.

incident-bot: Auto-mitigation triggered: route-replace jobs completed (job id 98765).

Maria: starting incident timeline + customer impact note. Draft snippet: "We observed increased latency and partial streaming stalls for sessions in eu-west-2 due to cross-AZ NAT instability. Immediate mitigation: traffic rebalanced to newly-provisioned NAT gateways; further network diagnostics are ongoing. Root cause investigation in progress."

Emily: Good. Who's doing root cause? @Raj + @Kevin for networking, @Maria for impact and comms.

Raj: collecting packet captures and VPC flow logs for window 1820043000-1820045800. Initial look shows bursts of ICMP fragmentation and out-of-order segments between az-b <-> az-c. Could be transient switch-level congestion or an MTU mismatch after a config push.

Kevin: I pulled hypervisor logs — noisy interface errors on host fleet in az-b cluster 12 around 09:12 UTC. I've flagged hosts and started migration of NAT instances off those hosts.

Maria: Ops note — two Dedicated customers reported degraded realtime transcription quality; they've been informed via support ticket with incident ref INC-2026-345. Added to incident timeline.

Emily: Handoff — I'm going offline in 10m. Maria, taking lead. Raj/Kevin continue root cause. Maria, call if we need escalation.

Maria: taking over incident lead. Oncall handoff: "Emily -> Maria" (confirmed). Updating runbook.

sre-runbook-bot: runbook step executed: Increase NAT ephemeral port range and enable conntrack tweaks. Commands applied: 
```
echo 1024 65535 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
```

Kevin: made conntrack increase and ephemeral range change across nat fleet. Conntrack saturation metrics down. No further RST surges. p99 now 1.8s and falling.

Raj: still seeing intermittent tail jitter but much improved. Flow logs show reduced packet loss. Marking network mitigation as successful for now.

Maria: Customer impact update being posted to status.redwood.ai: "Partial streaming degradation in eu-west-2 between 09:10–09:40 UTC. Mitigation applied; some customers experienced higher latency or stream resets. Continued monitoring."

Emily: (checked in via DM) if anything regresses, call page again. otherwise we transition to postmortem and RCA.

Kevin: I'll open a follow-up to coordinate with cloud provider support for host-level interface errors and check BGP/underlay alarms.

Raj: grabbing relevant logs for RCA: config change history, switch-level alarms, and flow logs. Will include packet captures and timeline.

Maria: Confirmed last_message_ts 1820046050. Current action items: 
- Kevin: provider escalation + host remediation (assigned)
- Raj: RCA draft + packet captures (assigned)
- Maria: customer comms + post-incident status (assigned)
- Emily: postmortem owner (will triage in next shift)

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-345 status: Mitigated -> monitoring. P1 -> P2.

Emily: thanks team. Leaving channel. :white_check_mark:

Maria: closing incident bridge in 15m unless we see regression. Keeping channel open for follow-ups.

Kevin: uploading NAT host logs to /mnt/incident-logs/INC-2026-345/ for RCA.

Raj: I'll start the RCA doc and link to logs. Expect first draft in 24h.

Maria: ack. I'll update customer list and SLA calc.

incident-bot: This thread will be archived when the incident is resolved.
